rules.title: Limit on payments at or before start of tenancy
rules.requirement: At or prior to the start of a tenancy, a lessor or agent of the lessor may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.
rules.key_value: first month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit equal to first month's rent, and key and lock cost
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential real property and their agents, for tenants and prospective tenants.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(1)(b)
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent, and must be deposited as required by subsection (3) with the tenant given a statement of condition. If a fee in lieu of a security deposit is authorized by regulation, the fees plus any deposit may not exceed, in total, 1 month's rent.
rules.key_value: equal to the first month's rent
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential real property and their agents.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(1)(b)(iii)
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

rules.title: Security deposit receipt
rules.requirement: A lessor or agent who receives a security deposit must give a signed receipt stating the amount, the name of the person receiving it (and lessor if an agent), the date received, and a description of the premises.
rules.coverage_text: Any lessor or agent receiving a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(2)(b)
rules.quoted_span: (b) Any lessor or his agent who receives a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall give said tenant or prospective tenant at the time of receiving such security deposit a receipt indicating the amount of such security deposit, the name of the person receiving it and, in the case of an agent, the name of the lessor for whom such security deposit is received, the date on which it is received, and a description of the premises leased or rented.

rules.title: Statement of condition
rules.requirement: A lessor who accepts a security deposit must, upon receipt or within ten days after the tenancy begins, whichever is later, give the tenant a separate signed written statement of the present condition of the premises including existing damage.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential real property or their agents who accept a security deposit.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(2)(c)
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.

rules.title: Separate interest-bearing account for deposits
rules.requirement: A security deposit must be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank in the commonwealth, protected from the lessor's creditors, and the tenant must receive a receipt with the bank name, location, amount and account number within thirty days.
rules.coverage_text: Any lessor receiving a security deposit.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(3)(a)
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with this paragraph shall entitle the tenant to immediate return of the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.

rules.title: Interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: A lessor holding a security deposit for one year or longer must pay the tenant interest at five per cent per year, or the lesser amount received from the bank, at the end of each year of tenancy, with an annual statement.
rules.key_value: five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank
rules.coverage_text: Lessors of residential real property holding a security deposit for one year or longer.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(3)(b)
rules.penalty: If the tenant has not received the notice or payment after thirty days from the end of each year, the tenant may deduct the interest due from the next rent payment.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Return of security deposit
rules.requirement: The lessor must return the security deposit or its balance within thirty days after the tenancy ends, deducting only unpaid rent or water charges, certain unpaid tax increases, and reasonable damage repair costs (excluding reasonable wear and tear) with a sworn itemized list.
rules.key_value: within thirty days after the termination of occupancy
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(4)
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit to successor
rules.requirement: A lessor who transfers interest in the unit must transfer the security deposit with accrued interest to the successor, who must notify the tenant in writing within forty-five days of the transfer.
rules.coverage_text: Lessors who transfer their interest in a dwelling unit for which a security deposit is held, and their successors in interest.
rules.exemptions: The granting of a mortgage is not a transfer of interest. Successor liability does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter sixty or to a foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession which is a financial institution chartered by the commonwealth or the United States.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(5)
rules.quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such security deposit that such security deposit was transferred to him and that he is holding said security deposit.

rules.title: Forfeiture of right to retain security deposit
rules.requirement: A lessor forfeits the right to keep any part of the security deposit, or to counterclaim for damage, if the lessor fails to deposit it as required, fails to give an itemized damage list within thirty days, uses conflicting lease provisions or seeks a waiver, fails to transfer it, or fails to return it within thirty days after the tenancy ends.
rules.citation: General Laws Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 15B(6)
rules.penalty: The lessor shall forfeit his right to retain any portion of the security deposit for any reason, or to counterclaim for any damage to the premises in a tenant's action to recover the deposit.
